title: FSD P10 v3 publishes the agent dashboard through a data lake write and Power BI, both removed by Architecture v5
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.2, A2.6.4.1 and AC-EXC-P10-006-01; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 13, 37 and 44; Story Template and Rules v1 DP-17
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.6 publish the agent monitoring dashboard, integration points and acceptance criteria; BRD Program v5 section 6.12
description: FSD P10 v3 has the agent monitoring dashboard built by a nightly job that writes to the data lake and is read by Power BI, and its exception criterion checks the row count of the data lake write. Architecture v5 states that the Workbench never connects to the data lake, that the Power BI connection and INT-19 and INT-20 are removed, and that reporting is a read model built from events into rwb-reporting. The two statements cannot both hold.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 A2.6.2: integration points Power BI and model gateway. AC-EXC-P10-006-01: the data lake write for 2026-12-01 stores 1 row for 2 agent and version groups, so the publish is held. Arch v5 slide 8: no data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed). Slide 13: reporting reads projections, not a lake. Slide 37 and DP-17: the reporting extract is built by rwb-reporting from its own projections.
proposed: Architecture v5 wins under R-PREC rule 1. The dashboard is served on screen SCR-46 from the service's own daily measures and from the read model of rwb-reporting; no lake file, lake row, Power BI data set or lake delivery exists, and the row-count check is made on the measure hand-over instead of the lake write.

title: The daily aggregate table the FSD acceptance criteria name is not in the Logical Data Model v8 entity list
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-ALT-P10-006-02 and AC-EXC-P10-006-01; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 entity list; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.6 acceptance criteria; LDM v8 agent runtime entities; Ownership Map Tables
description: The FSD acceptance criteria of A2.6 assert that agent_run_daily holds the same two rows for a business date after a rerun. The Logical Data Model v8 lists eight agent runtime entities (agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation, agent_feedback, agent_alert) and does not list agent_run_daily. The Ownership Map gives the same eight tables to P10. A table asserted by an acceptance criterion and absent from the data model cannot be built without a decision.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 AC-ALT-P10-006-02: agent_run_daily holds the same 2 rows for 2026-12-01. LDM v8 entity rows AGT: eight entities, no daily aggregate. Ownership Map Tables: eight P10 rows.
proposed: The daily measure is read as a projection over the run record for the business date, produced once per agent and version and idempotent on the date. Its physical name and retention are the technical specification's; the PRD states only the measure and the once-per-date rule.

title: FSD P10 v3 has the agent read ACE and case facts directly, while Architecture v5 and ADR-010 reserve every ACE read to rwb-source-data
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.1, A2.3, A2.10 description integration points, A2.11 description; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 9, 16 and 29; ADR-010; D-RCV-35 U4; DP-05
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.1.2, A2.3.2, A2.10.2 and A2.11.2 integration points; BRD Program v5 section 6.3
description: The FSD names ACE as an integration point of the agent platform, of the intake shadow run, of the TDR suggestion and of the fallback, and its integration list is the model gateway plus ACE, the Workbench or TDR. Architecture v5 states that only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views, that no other service holds a grant on the recovery schema, and that the agent reaches case facts with a read-only tool. A direct ACE read by rwb-agent would breach the service boundary.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 A2.1.2: integration points model gateway, ACE. A2.10.2: model gateway, ACE and TDR. Arch v5 slide 9: only rwb-source-data reads the SQL views. Slide 16: rwb-agent out, REST source data as a tool to read case facts and document as a tool to read extracted fields. Slide 29: one login per schema, no cross-schema grant.
proposed: The PRD requires every case fact to be read through the rwb-source-data tool contract, one hop with a 2 s budget, and every extracted document field through the rwb-document tool contract, and forbids any grant of rwb_agent on the recovery schema or on another service schema.

title: JOB-15 is the reporting extract of rwb-reporting in the Ownership Map, but the FSD uses its completion as the trigger of the P10 dashboard
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-ALT-P10-006-01, AC-ALT-P10-006-02 and AC-EXC-P10-006-02; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-15; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.6 acceptance criteria; Ownership Map Jobs; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 jobs table
description: The FSD fires the cost alert and writes the daily measures when JOB-15 completes, and the Batch and Scheduling Design v4 defines JOB-15 as the 01:30 reporting extract that writes case, queue, decision and outcome data. The Ownership Map gives JOB-15 to P9 rwb-reporting with an Airflow trigger and no data lake. P10 therefore has either no trigger for its own aggregation or a schedule it does not own.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 AC-ALT-P10-006-01: JOB-15 completes for 2026-12-01, then one alert row exists. Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-15: reporting extract, nightly 01:30, owner reporting and BI analyst. Ownership Map Jobs: JOB-15 owner P9, replacement Airflow trigger buildRegulatoryExtract in rwb-reporting, no data lake. Arch v5 slide 44: JOB-15 owner rwb-reporting.
proposed: The Ownership Map wins. JOB-15 stays the reporting extract of rwb-reporting. The PRD gives rwb-agent its own daily aggregation step, triggered once per business date after the run record closes, and the measures are handed to rwb-reporting for the read model. The PRD names no job ID for it because no ID is free.

title: The admin configuration paths differ between the FSD and Architecture v5, and no source states the service REST base explicitly
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-EXC-P10-001-02, AC-ALT-P10-001-01, AC-EXC-P10-010-01; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 API sheet; Story Template and Rules v1 DP-13
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.1 and A2.6 acceptance criteria; Arch v5 slide 16 P10 contract; Ownership Map API
description: The FSD names POST /admin/agent-configs, GET /admin/agent-configs, POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve, POST /admin/agent-samples and the evaluation and metric paths. Architecture v5 slide 16 names GET/POST /agent-policies (admin) and GET /agent-runs/{id}. The Ownership Map lists the FSD paths under P10. The service base /api/recovery/agent/v1 follows DP-13 but is not written in the P10 sources.
evidence: FSD P10 v3: the twelve paths of the admin and case reads. Arch v5 slide 16: REST GET /agent-runs/{id}, GET/POST /agent-policies (admin). Ownership Map API: twelve P10 rows, x-module P10. Story Template and Rules DP-13: /api/recovery/v1 becomes /api/recovery/<short>/v1.
proposed: The PRD states the base path and the operations in product terms only and leaves the exact path names to the service contract, which the API Specification v4 and the Ownership Map carry. The named paths in the FSD stay the behavioural reference.

title: The P10 message codes are referenced in the acceptance criteria but their wording is in no source document
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-EXC-P10-001-02, AC-EXC-P10-001-05, AC-EXC-P10-001-06, AC-ALT-P10-006-01, AC-ALT-P10-007-02, AC-EXC-P10-010-01 and AC-EXC-P10-010-02; FSD P10 v3 Appendix B
description: The acceptance criteria refuse a failed configuration load with MSG-P10-001, an empty sample with MSG-P10-002, a concurrent evaluation with MSG-P10-003, a cost cap with MSG-P10-004, an unavailable TDR suggestion with MSG-P10-007 and an unfinished evaluation report with MSG-P10-008. No document in the source set states the wording of MSG-P10-001 to MSG-P10-008, and Appendix B refers only to the Error and Message Standard.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 cites MSG-P10-001, 002, 003, 004, 007 and 008 without text. The other module FSDs and the message standard are not in the source set for this work package. Appendix B: message wording follows the Error and Message Standard.
proposed: The PRD refers to the codes and to the message that the source names, and states no wording. The wording is taken from the Error and Message Standard at build time; a code with no entry there is a defect of the message standard and not of this PRD.

title: The FSD P10 requirement table is empty, so no FSD requirement ID exists to map a product requirement to
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 section Requirements served; FSD P10 v3 A2.1 to A2.16; Story Template and Rules v1 R7.3 fill order
section: FSD P10 v3 Requirements served table
description: The Requirements served table of FSD P10 v3 holds its heading and no row, so no requirement ID exists for any of the sixteen features the document describes. Every other mapping in the PRD therefore names the FSD section and its acceptance criteria instead of a requirement ID, and a reader cannot trace an FR to a single FSD requirement key.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 document section Requirements served: three column headings and no row. The feature table of A1.2 names sixteen features FEAT-AGT-01 to FEAT-AGT-16 and none of them has a requirement key.
proposed: This PRD maps each FR to the FSD section and acceptance criteria it serves, and to the feature code where the FSD carries one. The FSD is asked to fill its Requirements served table in its next version; no requirement ID is invented here.

title: No target exists for agent acceptance, override, latency and cost, and no evidence or threshold exists for an autonomy change
source: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 KPI-012, Q-014, Q-026 and ASM-021; BRD Program v5 NFR-066 and NFR-010; FSD P10 v3 A2.13 and A2.15
section: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 10 measures and section 11 questions; BRD Program v5 section 6.12; FSD P10 v3 A2.13 and A2.15
description: The BRD measures agent acceptance, override, latency and cost per agent and states that no target applies until one is set (KPI-012, Q-026). It leaves the measured evidence and threshold that justify a change of autonomy level open (Q-014, ASM-021). The FSD requires a drift threshold and a minimum feedback on the policy row and a proposal that meets every stated condition, but names no value. The only numeric target in the source set is the 10 percent fallback rate of the FSD intent table.
evidence: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 KPI-012: Measured per agent, no target. Q-026: what targets apply to agent acceptance, override rate, latency and cost. Q-014: what measured evidence and threshold justify raising or lowering an autonomy level. FSD P10 v3 A2.1.1: fallback rate below 10 percent. A2.13: drift threshold and minimum feedback held on the policy row.
proposed: The PRD writes no value. The measures and the threshold are policy rows, the dashboard shows the measure, and the four targets stay open as Q-P10-01 and Q-P10-02 until Risk sets them. The fallback rate below 10 percent is carried as the one stated target.

title: No retention period is stated for an agent run, a guardrail result, a feedback row, an evaluation or a sample
source: FSD P10 v3 data entities and acceptance criteria; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 agent runtime entities; BRD Program v5 NFR-030, NFR-028 and NFR-031
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.1 to A2.16; BRD Program v5 section 6.5 retention; DL26
description: The service holds the record that proves what an agent answered, on which policy, prompt and model version, with which guardrail result and which fallback. No source states how long a run, a guardrail result, a feedback row, an evaluation run, a score row or a labeled sample is kept, and DL26 is open for the retention of every data product and document type.
evidence: BRD Program v5 NFR-030: the decision log is retained for the period the regulator and internal audit require, set by Compliance, open under DL26. NFR-031: case records carry a retention and archive rule by record class, not set. The LDM v8 agent runtime rows carry no retention column.
proposed: The PRD requires that the record is retained for the period set for it, is answerable to audit before a purge and is never removed silently, and writes the value as the R9 placeholder until Compliance sets it in DL26.

title: No date is stated for the platform wave that this service depends on
source: BRD Program v5 section 10.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38; Story Template and Rules v1 R5.6 and U7
section: BRD Program v5 section 10.3 waves and releases; PRD release slicing
description: Wave 0 of the program carries the seven platform epics and the non-functional integration epic, and the service cannot build before its template, libraries, schema, login, topic and gateway route exist. The BRD states the wave and no release date for it, and U7 forbids raising a date as a gap.
evidence: BRD Program v5 section 10.3: wave 0, platform and non-functional, before EP01, November 2026, no day stated. Arch v5 slide 38: the wave bands with the platform wave first.
proposed: The PRD writes the placeholder in the release date cell of the platform slice and states that no capability of this PRD starts before its platform enablers exist.

title: The BRD carries no status field and no approval record for the requirements approval gate
source: BRD Program v5 document control table and change log; BRD Epic 1 v5 document control; Story Template and Rules v1 R1 U8
section: BRD Program v5 section 1 document control; PRD section 13 approval
description: The PRD Builder precondition is an approved BRD with a Product Owner decision in a governance table. The BRD Program v5 document control table holds the document, the version, the date, the preparer, the tool, the coverage, the structure and two change rows, and no status and no approval. No governance decision row exists in any BRD of the set.
evidence: BRD Program v5 document control: eight rows, no status, no approval. Change log: version 4 and version 5 rows with author and tool only. Story Template and Rules U8: no human verification stop in this run.
proposed: The PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table and the gate is recorded as open. The assumption row states that the BRD is read as the approved baseline and that no story is blocked by it.

title: The Epic 2 legacy keys the FSD cites as the story of the feedback and legal pack criteria have no requirement row in the epic BRD
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-EXC-P10-007-02, AC-EXC-P10-008-02, AC-P10-009-01, AC-ALT-P10-009-01, AC-P10-010-01; BRD Epic 2 v3 section 3.10 and its gap CG-B-REQ-BRD-E2-4; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy
section: FSD P10 v3 story column; BRD Epic 2 v3 section 3.10 P10 Agent runtime
description: The FSD cites RWB-E2-028 and RWB-E2-029 as the story of the feedback and rejection criteria and RWB-E2-030 as the story of the legal document pack. BRD Epic 2 v3 section 3.10 holds two rows, RWB-E2-031 and RWB-E2-032, and its own gap CG-B-REQ-BRD-E2-4 records that ten keys including E2-028, E2-029 and E2-030 have no requirement row and are built from another source. The split plan nevertheless holds slices for all three.
evidence: BRD Epic 2 v3 section 3.10: RWB-E2-031 and RWB-E2-032 only. BRD Epic 2 v3 CG-B-REQ-BRD-E2-4: the ten keys with no requirement row here. split_plan legacy: RWB-E2-028, RWB-E2-029 and RWB-E2-030 with wave 2 and P10 slices.
proposed: The PRD cites the three keys as the legacy story of the capability and traces the product requirement to the BRD requirement it serves, so the missing requirement row does not change what is built. The epic BRD is asked to add the three rows in its next version.

title: The tool gateway is stated as read-only and the guardrail is stated against an allowed action list, without saying whether an agent may ever act
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 35; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.2 description and A2.6.3.2 allowed_tools; BRD Program v5 REQ-CWC-017 and REQ-CWC-018
section: Arch v5 slide 16 P10 contract; FSD P10 v3 A2.2 and the field catalog of A2.6.3.2
description: Architecture v5 gives P10 a tool gateway of read-only calls for the agent and the rule that AI suggests and never decides. The FSD tests every answer against an allowed action list held on the policy row and the BRD requires an agent that writes to a queue to pass the same checks as a person. Read-only tools and an allowed action list describe two different degrees of freedom and no source says which one holds.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 16: Tool gateway, read-only calls for the agent. Slide 35: suggests, never decides, a person approves. FSD P10 v3 A2.2: the allowed action list. A2.6.3.2: agent_policy.allowed_tools, tools the agent may call through the tool gateway. BRD Program v5 REQ-CWC-018: a model or agent writing to a queue passes the same permission checks as a person.
proposed: The PRD requires a read-only tool gateway for the whole of wave 1 and wave 2 and treats the allowed tool list as an allow list that can only narrow what a run may read. A write tool is named as an open question and not as a requirement.

title: The agent monitor screen is named with no screen specification in the source set
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 section Screens and A2.6; BRD Epic 1 v5 RWB-E1-063; BRD Epic 2 v3 RWB-E2-031
section: FSD P10 v3 Screens table; PRD section 11 AC on the monitor
description: The FSD names one screen, SCR-46 Agent monitor, and describes its content only through the acceptance criteria of A2.6 and through the field catalog of the policy row. No screen specification, component list, state list or message placement exists for it in the source set, so the product behaviour of the screen can be stated and its layout cannot.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 Screens: SCR-46 Agent monitor, agent runs, fallbacks, evaluation results and autonomy levels, first in E2 and full in E8. BRD Epic 1 v5 RWB-E1-063: a dashboard with acceptance, override, latency and cost per agent and version. Appendix B: components and states follow the Design System and Component Library.
proposed: The PRD states what the screen shows and that every measure is filtered by agent, policy version, prompt version and business date, and leaves the layout to the design system and the story set.

title: Four P10 features carry the same main success criterion, so the criterion does not distinguish the feature it belongs to
section: FSD P10 v3 main success and alternate flow tables of A2.1, A2.2, A2.5 and A2.11
description: The platform set-up, the guardrail checker, the evaluation harness and the rule fallback each carry the same approved-endpoint run criterion, the same prompt-version criterion and the same schema-check criterion, and each also carries the same six exception criteria. One criterion cannot be the evidence of four different features, and a reader cannot tell from the criterion which feature accepts it.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 AC-P10-001-01, AC-P10-002-01, AC-P10-005-01 and AC-P10-011-01 are identical in text. AC-ALT-P10-001-01, 002-01, 005-01 and 011-01 are identical. The exception sets of the four features are identical too.
proposed: The PRD keeps the criteria that are stated once and gives each feature the criterion that shows its own behaviour: the guardrail rejects, the fallback returns the rule result, the harness scores, and the platform set-up produces the run row and the event. The repeated source criteria stay as the shared background.

title: The boundary of the TDR suggestion message is not defined between rwb-agent and the treatment screen
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-EXC-P10-010-01, AC-EXC-P10-010-02, AC-ALT-P10-010-01; Arch v5 slide 16 P10 contract
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.10 acceptance criteria; SCR-14 treatment screen
description: The FSD shows MSG-P10-007 on SCR-14 when no suggestion is available, and shows the suggestion provenance on the same screen. SCR-14 is the treatment screen of S2 rwb-treatment and the message code is a P10 code. No source states which service owns the message, which wording it carries or whether the treatment screen shows a reason at all.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 AC-EXC-P10-010-01: SCR-14 shows MSG-P10-007 and no decision log entry is written. AC-ALT-P10-010-01: SCR-14 shows Suggested by TDR_OFFER, version TDR-OFFER-1.0. Arch v5 slide 16: P10 exposes the gateway call, S2 owns the treatment record and its screen.
proposed: The PRD requires that a caller learns that no suggestion is available and why, in the terms of the outcome the service recorded, and leaves the screen, the wording and the message ownership to the treatment PRD and the message standard.

title: The screening feature is titled at L1 and its main criterion stores a shadow run that creates no deviation
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.8 heading, A2.8.1, AC-P10-008-01 and AC-ALT-P10-008-01; FSD P10 v3 A1.2 feature table row FEAT-AGT-08; BRD Epic 1 v5 RWB-E1-062
section: FSD P10 v3 A2.8 run the deviation screening agent at L1; BRD Epic 1 v5 section 3.9
description: The A2.8 heading and intent say the screening agent is put live on one segment at autonomy level 1, and its main acceptance criterion asserts that each run stores its proposed codes in mode SHADOW, that no deviation record exists, that deviation_open stays false on every case and that no contact stop is set. The epic BRD places RWB-E1-062 in Epic 1 as a shadow run. The heading and the criterion describe two different modes.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 A2.8.1: puts the screening agent live on one segment at autonomy level 1. AC-P10-008-01: each run stores its proposed codes in mode SHADOW and no deviation record exists. A1.2: FEAT-AGT-08 run the deviation screening agent at L1, first in E2. BRD Epic 1 v5 RWB-E1-062: the deviation screening agent flagging X1 to X7 in shadow on Epic 1 data.
proposed: The mode is read from the policy row and one code path serves both, which is how the intake agent is described in A2.7: the shadow run of Epic 1 is the same run with mode SHADOW, and the L1 run of Epic 2 hands the proposal to rwb-deviation through that owner's contract.

title: The FSD states no wave or release for any of the sixteen agent features
source: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A1.2 feature overview and section 1 module table; BRD Program v5 sections 8 and 10.3; Story Template and Rules v1 R5.6
section: FSD P10 v3 feature overview first-in column; BRD Program v5 release plan
description: The FSD gives each agent feature a first-in epic (E1, E2, E3 or E8) and no wave and no date. The wave map of the rules turns an epic into a wave and the BRD release plan gives each wave its tentative date, so the PRD takes the BRD plan. The two sources agree on the epic and neither states a wave in the agent document.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 A1.2: first in E1, E2, E3 or E8. Story Template and Rules R5.6: EP01 wave 1, EP02 and EP03 wave 2, EP06 to EP08 wave 4. BRD Program v5 section 8: eight release dates, tentative.
proposed: The PRD slices by wave from the epic of each feature, takes the dates from BRD Program v5 section 8 unchanged and marks every date tentative.
